correctness.rationale: A Kneser total-dominating subset is exactly an edge family of K_n with no two-point vertex cover. Every degree-at-least-three vertex belongs to any two-cover. Exhaustive disjoint cases with zero, one, or two such vertices yield the C,H,Q formulas. A two-covered family with at least n+1 edges has two mandatory high-degree hubs and therefore a unique two-cover, giving binomial(n,2)*binomial(2n-3,k) exact failures. Python and an independent C program directly enumerate every subset for n=3..7 (2,131,016 total), matching all coefficients; these finite checks corroborate but do not replace the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The complete cardinality distribution for all KG(n,2) at n≥6, rather than merely minimums or the published order-five example, is a natural graph invariant. An exact zero/one/two-high-degree-hub decomposition yields computable all-order coefficients. The entire interior unique-transversal band n+1≤k≤2n−4 is a nontrivial extension of the previously known topmost regular-graph coefficients and clarifies why overlap disappears far below the domination cutoff. No novelty is claimed for the pre-existing n=5 polynomial or the universal top cutoff.
